intro: Every plant in the botanic garden's glasshouse bloomed on the same night, and the labels in the pots had all been rewritten. The gardeners arrived to find the glasshouse full of unfamiliar names, though the horticulture matched each pot exactly—one familiar and one foreign, side by side, as if the plants had signed in twice. Head gardener Marlowe asked them to collect the labels and set the odd ones aside, and the shed wall now holds eight neat rows of paper, each row carrying one letter folded into its neighbour. She said the extra letters would not go to waste, and that when the time came, they would read in the order the rows were pinned. The glasshouse has not stopped blooming, and still no one has found the gardener who did the pinning.
echo: Pull it from the soil and its scream, they say, will kill you.

puzzles.title: Photoperiod
puzzles.flavor: Pairs of numbers pencilled in the margin.

hints: The first number in each pair never goes past the number of words on the page. What does the second count?
The first number finds a word on the page; the second finds a letter in it.

puzzles.title: Cross-Pollination
puzzles.flavor: Numbers that nothing divides, written the old way.

partials.f6a5a18998391f022bdeb6ed366e8e6694e69711: Nearly. There's a stowaway aboard: one letter too many. Put it ashore, but remember who it was.

hints: Read the numerals. They're all prime. Is there a natural way to number the primes?
Find each prime's place in the list of primes (2 is 1st, 3 is 2nd…), then count through the alphabet.

partials.61a202cbcbaab6c22d4ecf3dc4103d48cfe69a51: Nearly. There's a stowaway aboard: one letter too many. Put it ashore, but remember who it was.

hints: Once every theme word is found, is anything left unclaimed? Read it in order.
Find the theme words; the letters no word uses, read row by row, are the answer.
The hidden words are: BARK, BULB, FERN, LEAF, MOSS, ROOT, SEED, SPORE, STEM, STOMA, THORN.
